Dunleavy is term-limited after two terms. Alaska leans R but uses ranked-choice voting, introducing uncertainty.
Hobbs won by only 0.6% in 2022. Arizona is a premier presidential battleground making this a top toss-up.
Sanders won by 65 points in 2022. Arkansas is a deep Republican state.
Newsom is term-limited. California is solidly Democratic; the Democratic nominee is heavily favored.
Polis is term-limited. Colorado has trended solidly Democratic in recent cycles.
Lamont re-elected in 2022. Connecticut is a reliably Democratic state.
DeSantis is term-limited. Florida has shifted rightward but an open seat adds some uncertainty.
Kemp is term-limited. Georgia is a top battleground; the open seat makes this a competitive race.
Hawaii is one of the most Democratic states in the country. Green won easily in 2022.
Idaho is a deep Republican state. Little won re-election comfortably in 2022.
Pritzker is eligible for a third term. Illinois is solidly Democratic at the statewide level.

Kelly is term-limited. Kansas is a reliably Republican state and is expected to flip back to the GOP.
Mills is term-limited. Maine is competitive and uses ranked-choice voting; leans Democratic.
Moore won by 33 points in 2022. Maryland is a deep blue state.
Healey won by 29 points in 2022. Massachusetts is one of the most Democratic states.
Whitmer is term-limited. Michigan is the premier governor battleground of 2026 — a genuine toss-up open seat.
Walz will not seek re-election after his 2024 VP run. Minnesota leans Democratic in statewide races.
Nebraska is a deep Republican state. Pillen won easily in 2022.
Lombardo is a Republican incumbent in a purple state that has voted Democratic in presidential races. Key toss-up.
Ayotte won the 2024 race (2-year term). NH is competitive but Ayotte has strong crossover appeal.
Michelle Lujan Grisham is term-limited. New Mexico has trended Democratic and the nominee is favored.
Hochul survived a competitive 2022 race. New York leans heavily Democratic in statewide races.
DeWine is term-limited. Ohio has shifted Republican but the open seat could draw strong Democratic challengers.
Stitt is term-limited. Oklahoma is a deep Republican state with no competitive race expected.
Kotek won narrowly in a 3-way 2022 race. Oregon trends Democratic, especially in a two-party contest.
Shapiro won by 15 points in 2022. Pennsylvania is a key swing state with a strong Democratic incumbent.
Rhode Island is a deep blue state. Republicans have not won the governorship since 2010.
McMaster re-elected by 12 points in 2022. South Carolina is a reliably Republican state.
Noem is term-limited. South Dakota is a deep Republican state with no competitive race expected.
Lee is term-limited. Tennessee is a deep Republican state with no competitive race expected.
Abbott won by 11 points in 2022. Texas is reliably Republican at the statewide level.
Scott wins by 40+ points in a deep blue state — uniquely popular. Vermont holds 2-year governor terms.
Wisconsin is the ultimate national battleground. Evers narrowly won in both 2018 and 2022.
Gordon is term-limited. Wyoming is one of the most Republican states in the nation.

path_to_majority.summary: Republicans currently hold 27 governorships vs. Democrats 23. Of the 36 races in 2026, 18 lean Republican, 14 lean Democratic, and 4 are toss-ups. The key open seats in Michigan, Georgia, and Kansas, plus incumbent battles in Arizona and Wisconsin, will define the 2026 governor map.

midterms.context: First-term Clinton backlash. Republicans ran a unified Contract with America platform. Healthcare reform failure energised conservatives. Democrats lost 54 seats — largest loss since 1946.
Only second time since WWII that the president's party gained House seats in midterms. Republican impeachment of Clinton backfired. Booming economy and Clinton's 66% approval drove Democratic gains.

midterms.context: Iraq War dominated the election. Mark Foley congressional page scandal broke weeks before Election Day. Nancy Pelosi became the first female Speaker. Democrats flipped both chambers simultaneously for the first time since 1986.

Largest House swing since 1938 and the biggest midterm loss since Truman in 1946. 9.8% unemployment and ACA backlash fuelled the Tea Party movement. Census-year election gave Republicans sweeping redistricting power for a decade.

Second-term Obama drag. Oct 2013 government shutdown initially hurt Republicans but Democrats couldn't capitalise. Record-low turnout of 36.4%. Republicans flipped the Senate for the first time since 2006. Ebola fears and ISIS dominated the final weeks.

Democrats flipped 41 House seats driven by suburban college-educated women voters. The economy was strong but anti-Trump sentiment dominated. Republicans held and expanded Senate majority in a very favourable map — only 9 R seats vs 26 D seats up for election.

Expected red wave failed to materialise. Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade energised Democratic turnout especially among women and young voters. Republicans eked out a 9-seat House majority but significantly underperformed polling. Democrats gained a Senate seat in Pennsylvania.
